class.name: VAOpenALSettings
class.description: Global OpenAL device and mixer settings. Add exactly one of these anywhere in the scene tree (an autoload is the natural place).

method.name: get_available_devices
method.description: Returns the names of the playback devices currently available on this machine.

method.name: refresh_devices
method.description: Re-queries the driver's list of available playback devices, so a device plugged in after this node was selected in the editor shows up in [member device_name]'s dropdown without reselecting the node or restarting the editor.

members.member: The playback device to use. Leave empty to use the driver's default device.
The maximum number of auxiliary reverb sends available per source. 0 leaves this at the driver's default.
The overall output volume, as a linear multiplier. 1.0 is unchanged, 0.0 is silent.
The mixing sample rate, in Hz. "Driver Default" (0) leaves this at the driver's default.
If [code]true[/code], requests HRTF-based binaural rendering instead of the driver's default panning. The driver can still refuse, e.g. if it has no HRTF data for the current output device.

How volume attenuates with distance from the listener. One of OpenAL's distance model constants (Inverse Distance Clamped, Inverse Distance, Linear Distance Clamped, Linear Distance, Exponent Distance Clamped, Exponent Distance, or None), selectable from the Inspector dropdown.

How many meters one world unit represents, for OpenAL's own air-absorption and reverb decay calculations. This is separate from [member VAWorld.meters_per_unit], which only affects vaudio's raytracing/acoustics model.
The speed of sound, in meters per second, used for OpenAL's Doppler effect calculation. This is separate from [member VAWorld.speed_of_sound], which only affects vaudio's raytracing/acoustics model.
If [code]true[/code], every sound's direct path is silenced so only reverb is audible. A diagnostic toggle for tuning reverb in isolation.
